The latest relevant reports describe Argentine enforcement actions in the **Argentine Exclusive Economic Zone**, but the available information does **not** establish that these events occurred in or near **Hermandad–Reserva Marina**:

- **Hai Xing 2:** Argentina reportedly fined the Chinese-origin vessel, sailing under the Tanzanian flag, nearly **1.9 billion pesos** for fishing maneuvers in the Gulf of San Jorge. The sanction was announced on **August 7, 2026**, based on vessel-tracking records; no boarding or detention was reported.
- **Bao Feng and Bao Win:** Two vessels linked to Chinese capital were reportedly fined more than **2.7 billion pesos** for illegal fishing in Argentina’s EEZ. The report says they could continue fishing in international waters; it does not report their detention.
- A separate article says **four foreign vessels** had been sanctioned in Argentina in 2026, but the supplied details identify only the Hai Xing 2 and the Bao Feng and Bao Win.

**No report provided mentions a vessel detention at Hermandad–Reserva Marina or confirms a connection between that reserve and these Argentine cases.**
mpas.rules_summary:
Hermandad is divided into two 30,000 km² zones:

- **No-take zone:** Extractive activities are prohibited.
- **Responsible-fishing zone:** Fishing is allowed, except fishing that uses longlines (palangre).

So, **fishing is not prohibited throughout the whole reserve**. The sources describe a no-take area and a separate area where fishing is permitted subject to the longline restriction; they do not establish that all commercial fishing is prohibited throughout Hermandad. The prohibition on all commercial fishing mentioned in one source applies to the **Galápagos Marine Reserve**, not specifically to Hermandad.

**Sources:** Ecuador’s Executive Decree and the zone rules are summarized by [Galápagos Conservancy](https://www.galapagos.org/newsroom/timeline-the-expansion-of-the-galapagos-marine-reserve/). The Ministry’s boundary update, Agreement MAATE-2022-041, was published in Ecuador’s *Registro Oficial* No. 59; its zones are summarized by [El Universo](https://www.eluniverso.com/noticias/politica/actualizacion-de-limites-de-la-reserva-marina-hermandad-se-publico-en-el-registro-oficial-nota/) and [Revista La Verdad](https://www.revista-laverdad.com/2022/05/11/actualizacion-de-limites-de-la-reserva-marina-hermandad-se-publico-en-el-registro-oficial/). Hermandad is divided into two 30,000 km² zones:

- **No-take zone:** Extractive activities are prohibited.
- **Responsible-fishing zone:** Fishing is allowed, except fishing that uses longlines (palangre).

So, **fishing is not prohibited throughout the whole reserve**. The sources describe a no-take area and a separate area where fishing is permitted subject to the longline restriction; they do not establish that all commercial fishing is prohibited throughout Hermandad. The prohibition on all commercial fishing mentioned in one source applies to the **Galápagos Marine Reserve**, not specifically to Hermandad.

**Sources:** Ecuador’s Executive Decree and the zone rules are summarized by [Galápagos Conservancy](https://www.galapagos.org/newsroom/timeline-the-expansion-of-the-galapagos-marine-reserve/). Hermandad is divided into two 30,000 km² zones:

- **No-take zone:** Extractive activities are prohibited.
- **Responsible-fishing zone:** Fishing is allowed, except fishing that uses longlines (palangre).

So, **fishing is not prohibited throughout the whole reserve**. The sources describe a no-take area and a separate area where fishing is permitted subject to the longline restriction; they do not establish that all commercial fishing is prohibited throughout Hermandad. The prohibition on all commercial fishing mentioned in one source applies to the **Galápagos Marine Reserve**, not specifically to Hermandad.

**Sources:** Ecuador’s Executive Decree and the zone rules are summarized by [Galápagos Conservancy](https://www.galapagos.org/newsroom/timeline-the-expansion-of-the-galapagos-marine-reserve/). The Ministry’s boundary update, Agreement MAATE-2022-041, was published in Ecuador’s *Registro Oficial* No. 59; its zones are summarized by [El Universo](https://www.eluniverso.com/noticias/politica/actualizacion-de-limites-de-la-reserva-marina-hermandad-se-publico-en-el-registro-oficial-nota/) and [Revista La Verdad](https://www.revista-laverdad.com/2022/05/11/actualizacion-de-limites-de-la-reserva-marina-hermandad-se-publico-en-el-registro-oficial/). mpa_rules.answer:
Hermandad is divided into two 30,000 km² zones:

- **No-take zone:** Extractive activities are prohibited.
- **Responsible-fishing zone:** Fishing is allowed, except fishing that uses longlines (palangre).

So, **fishing is not prohibited throughout the whole reserve**. The sources describe a no-take area and a separate area where fishing is permitted subject to the longline restriction; they do not establish that all commercial fishing is prohibited throughout Hermandad. The prohibition on all commercial fishing mentioned in one source applies to the **Galápagos Marine Reserve**, not specifically to Hermandad.

**Sources:** Ecuador’s Executive Decree and the zone rules are summarized by [Galápagos Conservancy](https://www.galapagos.org/newsroom/timeline-the-expansion-of-the-galapagos-marine-reserve/). The Ministry’s boundary update, Agreement MAATE-2022-041, was published in Ecuador’s *Registro Oficial* No. 59; its zones are summarized by [El Universo](https://www.eluniverso.com/noticias/politica/actualizacion-de-limites-de-la-reserva-marina-hermandad-se-publico-en-el-registro-oficial-nota/) and [Revista La Verdad](https://www.revista-laverdad.com/2022/05/11/actualizacion-de-limites-de-la-reserva-marina-hermandad-se-publico-en-el-registro-oficial/). **Summary:** The TUNAMAR, a Panama-flagged fishing vessel, was apparently involved in multiple fishing events within the Hermandad - Reserva Marina protected area in June 2026, and had a history of tracking gaps and fishing activities in the previous 12 months. The vessel's activities raised concerns due to its presence in a sensitive marine reserve.
## What happened
* 2026-06-01T02:36:00.000Z: Apparent fishing event started inside Hermandad - Reserva Marina

## Why it matters
The TUNAMAR's risk score is 35, indicating a low risk level, due to its apparent involvement in 3 fishing events inside the Hermandad - Reserva Marina, meeting or loitering with another vessel at sea (possible catch transfer), and a repeat pattern of 8 tracking gaps in the previous 12 months.
## Vessel background
The TUNAMAR is a Panama-flagged fishing vessel with IMO 7409138 and MMSI 355121000. Its owner is not explicitly stated, but its commercial manager is America Tower I Corp. In the 12 months prior to June 2026, the vessel had 8 tracking gaps, 10 fishing events, 0 encounters, 10 loitering events, and 7 port visits.
## What public sources say
The web search results indicate that TUNAMAR is identified as a Panama-flagged fishing vessel, but no reports of IUU fishing, sanctions, detentions, or fines were found [1]. The sources confirm its IMO and MMSI numbers and classify it as a fishing vessel. The Hermandad - Reserva Marina has rules prohibiting extractive activities in 30,000 km² of its area and allowing responsible fishing (excluding longline fishing) in another 30,000 km² [5][7].

There are no unknowns listed for this investigation.

1. Verify the TUNAMAR's AIS data for the events listed to confirm its presence and activities within the Hermandad - Reserva Marina.
